text:
The Capitals traded for Jordan Kyrou in June, sending a package built around Connor McMichael and the 16th pick of the 2026 draft to St. Louis, and so far they are getting a specialist. He has 14 points in 17 games, half of them on the power play, while playing only 14:33 a night.

The finishing is the part to doubt. He has 5 goals on 2.3 expected and is shooting 20%, double last season. But the luck cuts both ways: Washington has scored 5.7 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has quietly cost him assists. Over the last ten games he has 10 points against about 7 expected, so the two have not fully cancelled out.

What is missing is his own volume. His chances have dropped to 0.55 expected goals per 60 from 1.00 in St. Louis, where Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile at driving play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 95% of forwards. Watch his even-strength minutes; more of them is how the shots come back.
